comparator.route: Notarieel Recht, ordinary three-year bachelor; first-listed third-year metajuridical option
comparator.sourceNotes: The accessible September 2026 Dutch faculty OER, Annex VI Article 4 (printed pp.56–57), independently establishes the retained 180-EC Notarial Law structure: 60 EC year-one foundations, 60 EC second-year requirements, and 55 EC third-year requirements plus a restricted 5-EC metajuridical perspective/essay pair. The first-listed criminology option (4+1 EC) remains the neutral selected instance; other paired options are not stacked. The 5-EC thesis requires Academic Language Skills, Academic Skills and Academic Skills II; Private Law precedes Civil Law I/II, Civil Procedure, Business Law and Private International Law, and Criminal (Procedural) Law precedes the two later criminal-law units. The required noncredit first-year Tutoraat remains outside credit totals. The prospective pages are indicative 2027–2028 context, not binding current-year authority. The formerly stored August English EER URL returned 404 in the original audit; its historical availability is unverified, and it is replaced by the accessible current Dutch source and index. The ordinary full-time academic structure is retained; no new assertion about part-time pacing is made. External sources rechecked 2026-10-08; the original UCR no-match judgment and checkedOn date remain unchanged.
components: First-listed permitted metajuridical option, paired with its 1-EC criminology research essay; alternatives are Rechtsfilosofie or Rechtssociologie, each likewise 4+1 EC.
Academische vaardigheden III: metajuridisch onderzoek criminologie (essay)
Paired required essay for the selected criminology perspective; not an independent open elective.

routeSelection.route: Notarieel Recht, ordinary three-year bachelor; first-listed third-year metajuridical option
routeSelection.basis: The generic Notarial Law bachelor has a fixed 175-EC compulsory core and one 5-EC restricted third-year choice. The first-listed criminology perspective and its paired essay instantiate that choice without claiming it is mandatory for every student. The full-time three-year presentation avoids treating the separate part-time registration as an academic specialization.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: Legal foundations, interpretation, argument and research
Public, constitutional, administrative and criminal law
Private law, property, family relationships, succession and commercial transactions
adjacent: Business formation, accounting, finance and economic governance
Legal ethics, justice and the social operation of legal institutions
questions: How does law structure major life events, property and agreements between people?
How do legal and economic institutions shape businesses, taxation and cross-border transactions?

candidates.label: Law, public institutions & society
candidates.reason: The six available law subjects provide a meaningful legal core, but a separate public-law programme would require conflict, sustainability and other policy courses that are only adjacent to this notarial target. They do not supply another 24-course response with concrete contributions throughout.

alternatives.label: Private law, business & economic governance
alternatives.concept: Study private legal relationships, transnational business law, contracts, economic institutions, corporate finance, taxation and financial governance alongside the public, international and European legal foundations that frame them. This is the closest related-fields response to notarial interests, but it does not teach Dutch family, succession and property law, Dutch tax doctrine, civil procedure or notarial practice.
alternatives.labelReason: Seven law courses, seven economics/business courses, research methods, sociology, ethics and communication make private and commercial relationships the centre; the label does not imply Dutch notarial-law training.
progression: Law, Society & Justice precedes every dependent law course; Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations precedes Transnational Business Law and International Business & Governance; Research Methods & Statistics precedes advanced economics. All courses have exact planned offerings, and nine are at 300 level.
alternatives.distinctness: The route replaces comparative public institutions, conflict and social-movement courses with finance, microeconomics, econometrics and international business governance, a sustained response to private legal and commercial relationships rather than a change of label alone.

selection.assessment: Private law, business and economic governance is the strongest complete related-fields response to the target’s private-law, property, business and taxation orientation. A second public-law direction was tested but would need adjacent conflict, sustainability and general policy courses to reach 24 courses. Dutch family/succession law and notarial taxation cannot form separate routes because UCR lacks their specialist legal subjects and practice sequence. Production stops at one.

trace: Introduces definitions of law, the structure of legal systems and normative and social approaches to justice.
Studies human-rights instruments and case law as positive law and legal-philosophical questions.
Introduces enterprise formation and business planning, the institutional context in which business-law disputes arise.
Teaches sources, actors and obligations of public international law.
Studies comparative constitutional and administrative principles across legal systems.
Teaches empirical inquiry needed to examine law-in-society and regulatory outcomes; it is not doctrinal case-law method.
Teaches qualitative inquiry into legal institutions and social experiences of justice.
Studies criminal responsibility, legality, defences and justice systems.
Studies how legal institutions are embedded in social structures and inequality.
Explains corporate accounts and financial reporting implicated in business-law and accounting-law questions.
Studies EU legal sources, institutions and the operation of EU rules in domestic legal orders.
Teaches comparative cross-border business transactions, contract rules, intellectual property and dispute resolution.
Studies government taxation, redistribution and efficiency relevant to legal and fiscal policy.
Practises normative reasoning about justice and ethical legal decisions; it is not professional legal ethics training.
Teaches obligations in private relationships and transactions, including housing and other civil-law examples.
Studies civil society and social trust as contexts for legal institutions and their legitimacy.
Studies persuasive framing, public argument and ethical communication relevant to legal advocacy, without being a moot-court course.
Introduces international institutions and state relations that shape public international law.
Introduces market organisation and economic incentives behind commercial relationships.
Examines microeconomic choices, incentives and contracts shaping commercial interactions.
Studies political and institutional forces behind transnational business governance.
Teaches causal analysis of economic data that can evaluate business or regulatory effects, distinct from doctrinal legal research.
Studies banking, investment risk and financial decision-making as business contexts for financial regulation.

notes.text: Radboud Notarial Law is a Dutch-law degree with cumulative civil, family, succession, property-transfer and tax law, civil procedure, notarial professional regulation and a legal thesis. UCR can combine comparative private, business, criminal, constitutional, international and EU law with economics, finance, governance and ethics. These are related-fields programmes, not substitutes for Dutch notarial training or qualification.
